title: The First Car to Hit 100 km/h Was ELECTRIC (1899) ⚡🏁 #shorts

scenes.text: The first car to break one hundred kilometers an hour wasn't gas powered. It was electric.
In eighteen ninety-nine, the world speed record was a duel, and every car in it was electric.
Belgian racer Camille Jenatzy built a torpedo-shaped car and named it Never Satisfied.
Two electric motors, one for each rear wheel, and about half its weight was batteries.
On April twenty-ninth, near Paris, it hit almost one hundred and six kilometers an hour. That's sixty-six miles an hour.
The record stood for three years, until a steam car beat it. Then gas engines took over.
Electric was fastest first. So why did it take a century to come back? Follow EV Drive for daily car tech.
